paragraphs.text: A brick of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition), made from Yunnan leaf in 1990 and kept in Guangzhou’s tea trade through the decades since. Yunnan’s state factories only brought [wet piling](shou:wet-piling) into production in 1973, so this brick comes from the second decade of the style.
Thirty-six years on, it is far past the ten years after which the trade calls a ripe pu’er [aged](shou:age-aged). How it was kept has shaped it as much as the years have.

brewing.text: From a cake, brick or tuo, ease a piece off along the edge with a pick rather than snapping it, so the leaves stay whole. Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
